speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is customary for the Leader to do a wrap-up before we have a break.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The policies and strategies that we have debated and approved will help us navigate a world that is vastly different to the one we knew before the pandemic – a world that is much more complicated and unpredictable, characterised by slower growth, higher inflation, greater geopolitical contestations, fragmentation in the global economy and a looming climate crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2023 will enable us to adapt more nimbly to this changed world and to secure our future, anchored by a fair, sound and sustainable fiscal plan.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Against the backdrop of geopolitical tensions and an evolving world order, we reaffirmed the need to uphold international law and a rules-based multilateralism, whilst maintaining a strong defence to safeguard of sovereignty and security.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Russia's invasion of Ukraine serves as a continuing reminder that Singapore's sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, must never be taken for granted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the face of a looming climate crisis, this Budget builds on previous Budgets and reinforces our commitment to sustainability and strengthens Singapore's climate resilience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In Budget 2021, we unveiled the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In Budget 2022, we took bold steps to raise our national climate ambitions at a time when many countries were struggling to stay the course, including our move to increase the carbon tax.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2023 continues our efforts to work with our businesses, communities and individuals, with a view to achieving net zero by 2050.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Apart from climate resilience, we also discussed food resilience and how to diversify food imports, produce our own food and keep food affordable in the HDB heartlands.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members also spoke about the need for companies and workers to adjust to major structural shifts, including an accelerated green transition, digitalisation, greater economic nationalism and protectionism, and this brings about both opportunities and challenges.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This Budget focuses our efforts on helping businesses and workers ride the winds of change while helping them tide through this period of weaker growth and higher inflation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Recognising that economic transformation must go hand in hand with digitalisation, we reiterated the need to build an inclusive Smart Nation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We agreed to empower our people and businesses, especially the less digitally savvy to go digital with confidence in safe and secure online areas or spaces and to build stronger defences against scams, online harm and cybersecurity threats.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We recognise, as we always have, that the end goal of economic growth is to provide Singaporeans with good employment opportunities and wages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To that end, we supported the appointment of Jobs-Skills Integrators to better translate skills training into employment outcomes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To ensure no workers are left behind, we supported the Uplifting Employment Credit, the Enhanced Enabling Employment Credit and the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, and we agreed to protect all our workers by keeping the workplaces safe and inclusive and to safeguard their future by enhancing retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this Budget, we also rightly acknowledged the cooperation, hard work and sacrifices of everyone in our long fight against COVID-19, especially our healthcare workers who soldiered at the frontline of our pandemic response.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We considered how to protect and better support our healthcare workers in their careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also topped up the ComCare Endowment Fund to provide additional support to the lower-income families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Through our endorsement of these moves, we signalled to Singaporeans that they can be assured that we will see them through this challenging period of rising inflation and cost-of-living pressures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Families, marriage and parenthood took centrestage in this Budget and aptly so, given that the Budget Statement was delivered on Valentine's Day.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We increased the financial support for the early years of raising a child.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Minister in the Prime Minister's office, helping oversee marriage and parenthood measures, I also want to add that these measures are just the beginning of an important shift, where the whole-of-society moves to become one that values family well-being and supports caregiving, both for the young and the old and acts accordingly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We reaffirmed the critical role that early childhood education plays in a child's holistic development and agreed to close the gap in preschool enrollment rates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We will strengthen the multiple progression pathways in our education system and in our society.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Every year, there will be one Ministry that receives intense interest and the highest number of cuts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This year was no exception and this year the distinction went to the Ministry of National Development, not surprising with the high interest in housing issues.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Being a nature-loving nation, no animal was left behind either.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: From flats, we moved on to animated debate on rats, cats and cockerels.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This year did not see the appearance of otters or wild boars, but no doubt, they will find their way into future Budgets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Now, it remains put all our plans into action.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On this note, I would like to thank Members for their active participation and strong support over the past two weeks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And Mr Speaker, on behalf of this House, I would also like to express our appreciation to you and your deputies for presiding over the proceedings in a fair and even-handed manner, and ensuring the standing orders were observed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We are extremely grateful to the Clerk of Parliament, Deputy Clerk and the other Clerks of Parliament, the Parliament Secretariat and staff, interpreters and translators, all of whom have been working long hours, and tirelessly over the past fortnight to ensure that the proceedings went smoothly.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: What we do here will not be possible without the quiet work of so many behind the scenes, whether in big or small ways, it matters.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Similarly, as we set forth and translate these policies into action, the work of so many on the ground ensure that they are not just words, but deeds.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I had lunch yesterday with our KidSTART team, their families, the children under their Healthy with KidSTART "What's For Lunch?" series.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I was hugely encouraged by every parent I spoke to who found the programme so very useful to their parenting journey.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are grateful to our KidSTART practitioners, like Ms Pearl Goh whom I met, who visit them at home to work with them.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And we have partners, like Prudential, who sponsor important programmes like that, are providing food and nutrition for the families.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have folks like Huda Ali, who come onboard as host for cooking programmes, along with Chef Mazlan, to help families learn how to cook in nutritious and delicious ways, because families often think that healthy food equals expensive food.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But they actually go the extra mile too.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Huda, for example, brings her son to demonstrate how parents can involve their children when cooking at home, how to put into practice the techniques that are taught by KidSTART on conversing with their children during such activities.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We almost never see these actions and they go beyond the policies that we launch here.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And these folks play such critical roles to make sure that we are not just going through motions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is a significant strength of ours here in Singapore that we must never take for granted.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In many places, many of you who have lived and worked abroad, you will know that things do not always get realised.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, thank you to all who play an important role.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And this is natural and is to be expected.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We all have different views, needs and wants.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If you cast your eyes back to not just this Budget, but the Budgets preceding this – and certainly all the Budgets that I have presided over – there is really a lot more alignment than disagreement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Thirdly, I am struck by what Nominate Member of Parliament Mr Cheng Hsing Yao had just shared, and I believe there is a resonance with many, and his speech best listening to again, and to be read as well and with Leader's response.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are some valuable thoughts for all of us to ponder, what kind of Parliamentarians and leaders do we want to be here in this Chamber?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: What kind of leaders do we want as citizens, because how we respond and signal will shape the type of people we choose, and how they, in turn, choose to behave.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But notwithstanding that, I think we all here have choices to make too.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ee live in a very visual world, fueled by social media.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Policies are "tl;dr" – too long; did not read.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And if the form and style appeal, does that trump substance?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: If a person is deemed "cool", so does that mean that what he or she says must be right?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We see how this phenomenon manifests itself all around the world.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is an observation that I think we all note and see, but is this happening here as well?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And are we, as citizens, concerned enough to do something about it?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And if you need so, what exactly should we do?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Fifth, what are our thoughts on facts versus perceptions and emotions?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I shared last year, now I will say that again.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We live in a world where there is far more information than there has ever been in history.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And this will increase exponentially, but we are not necessarily better informed.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And truth be told, most of us do not often read everything.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And because we have such a high level of education.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are educated, we think we know, we scan, and we form opinions very quickly.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And if you touch your hearts, I think many of us could be guilty of that, too.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, storytelling is important, and we know it is an important tool and we use that quite regularly in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But we also know it is powerful because it stirs emotions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We have seen stories that are being shared that are, well, sometimes not quite true or half-true or presented without the proper context.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In Brexit, and I think has been clearly documented without dispute, how various parties on both ends, or on multiple ends, made campaign statements that are clearly false.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And they are real-life outcomes that result from this environment.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, again, we need to ask ourselves, should we be concerned?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do we do the hard right, or the easy wrong?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I believe that all of us know what the correct answer is and should be, but given the earlier few points that I mentioned and what we see happening around the world, what do we, as leaders in the political environment, what should we do?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do we pander to popular sentiments, knowing that it actually does work?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Or do we try to make what we believe would be right, but perhaps, a less popular decision?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Do we promised dreams that cannot be fulfilled, because we know that we do not have to actually do it for real?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And the truth is, this is probably the norm in most societies.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, the question again is, what do we want for our own society here in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For the seventh and last point, I think I will just want to end and say that I really do feel that our best days are ahead of us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Yes, we are, like every country, buffeted by the same pressures similar to many other societies and parliaments, and it can seem overwhelming.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When we look at the disruptions, we seem to be recovering from COVID-19, and then there is a war and high inflation, and so on.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And we also know that we are not perfect, because if we really want to nitpick, there are lots of things that we can criticise, either we do it publicly or we do it privately.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are many areas where we can improve, there are things that we can do better, and certainly, all of us can lead better.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But to be fair to ourselves, we are in not bad spot, we are in a decent place.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are not falling apart as a nation or as a society.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This did not happen by chance, and where we are, our standing, our reputation, the way we are valued and respected, all these have been achieved despite the limitations that we sometimes see in ourselves.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, the question is, can you imagine how much further we can go?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: How much better we can be, if we begin to iron out the kinks, if we begin to actively seek to improve and to develop better leaders at all levels, there are far greater heights that we can climb, and we can all do even better for our people and our nation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And that is what is before us here in Chamber.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And we are all part of this journey together.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Every Singaporean who plays their part, big or small, makes that difference.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, let us all do what we can.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Let us all just try our very best.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, I will do what is popular and raid the time reserves.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will generously take the Chair at 5.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.29 pm until 5.00 pm.
